orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: How do seasons affect milk turning into curd?
orchestrator_output.text_narration: Let's understand how milk changes into curd and how different seasons affect this process. Milk changes into curd because of tiny living things called bacteria. These bacteria are like tiny chefs! They eat the sugar in milk and turn it into an acid. This acid makes the milk thick and sour, turning it into curd. These tiny bacteria work best at a warm temperature. Not too hot, not too cold, just right! If it's too cold, they work very slowly. If it's too hot, they might not work well or even die. In summer, the weather is warm. This warm temperature is perfect for the bacteria to grow fast. So, milk turns into curd much quicker in summer, sometimes in just a few hours! But in winter, the weather is cold. The bacteria become slow and lazy in the cold. So, it takes a much longer time for milk to turn into curd in winter, sometimes even a whole day or more! So, the speed at which milk changes into curd depends a lot on the season because seasons change the temperature, and temperature affects how fast the bacteria work. This is a common change we see around us!
